USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Escalate tariffs on China to maximum levels. The US has overwhelming leverage in this trade war, with China's economy far more dependent on US markets than vice versa. The US should use this moment of economic strength to force comprehensive structural reforms on China's unfair trade practices, intellectual property theft, and market access barriers.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The evidence shows the US has significant leverage in this dispute. China's economy is heavily export-dependent, and the US is its largest market. The US trade deficit with China stands at $419 billion, giving the US substantial room to impose tariffs without proportionate retaliation. China's retaliatory tariffs on $110 billion of US goods are dwarfed by US tariffs on $250 billion of Chinese goods, and the US has threatened to tariff essentially all remaining imports (~$300 billion). China's stock market fell 25% in 2018 compared to only 6% for the Dow, demonstrating greater economic vulnerability. The IMF has flagged US-China trade tensions as contributing to weakened global expansion, but this affects China more given its export-oriented growth model. Senator Graham's assessment that 'this is the best chance in my lifetime to get China to change their cheating ways' reflects the strategic opportunity. The US should maintain maximum pressure to extract concessions on IP theft, forced technology transfer, and market access - issues that threaten long-term US competitiveness in AI, cloud computing, robotics, and green tech.
key_factors: US trade deficit with China at $419 billion provides leverage
China's stock market fell 25% in 2018 vs 6% for Dow, showing greater vulnerability
US has threatened tariffs on all remaining Chinese imports (~$300 billion)
China's retaliatory capacity limited to $110 billion vs US tariffs on $250 billion
Strategic opportunity to address IP theft and forced technology transfer in key future industries
IMF confirms trade tensions weakening global expansion, disproportionately affecting export-dependent China

sources_cited.source_id: www.bbc.com — Trade war: US-China trade battle in charts
sources_cited.excerpt: The US, which accuses China of unfair trading practices, launched a trade war against China last year. Not only does the US accuse China of stealing intellectual property, but it wants Beijing to make changes to its economic policies, which it says unfairly favour domestic companies through subsidies. The US also wants China to buy more US goods to rein in its lofty $419bn trade deficit with China

sources_cited.source_id: www.bbc.com — Trade war: US-China trade battle in charts
sources_cited.excerpt: In 2018, Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell more than 13% and the Shanghai Composite slumped nearly 25%. Both indices have recovered some ground this year and are up 12% and 16% respectively so far in 2019. By comparison, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell nearly 6% in 2018 and is already up some 11% this year

sources_cited.source_id: annenberg.usc.edu — Understanding the ongoing U.S.-China trade war
sources_cited.excerpt: The U.S. is concerned that while China has had ready access to the U.S. market and to invest in the U.S., American companies (and other foreign companies) are locked out of these markets in China. The worry is that if China can protect its companies from competition at home, it will be better able to compete with U.S. and other firms outside of China.
